# Authoring an event page

Read `SPEC.md` first. The reference page is `events/trenton.html`: copy its structure exactly.

## Files you own vs. shared files

**You create/edit only:**
- `events/<event-id>.html`: the page (id from `data/events.json`)
- `tools/geo/maps/<event-id>.json`: geo specs for your maps
- `data/geo/<map-id>.*`: generated by the build tool (map ids must start with `<event-id>-`, e.g. `long-island-flank`)

**Do NOT edit** (other agents work in parallel): `assets/**`, `data/events.json`, `data/places.json`, `index.html`, `tools/*.mjs`, `tools/geo/build.mjs`, `docs/`, other events' files.
If you need a change in a shared file (library feature, bug, wrong event summary or coordinates, a place worth adding to the gazetteer), **don't make it**: list it in your final report.

## Workflow per page

1. **Research** the event from reputable sources: NPS, American Battlefield Trust (battlefields.org), Journal of the American Revolution, Mount Vernon's encyclopedia, Wikipedia plus its cited sources. Get positions, routes, dates and times right. Know what Chernow's book covers (see `PLAN.md`), but **never quote the book**. All text is your own words.
2. **Plan maps.** 1–4 per page, each showing one aspect that a reader of the book would otherwise look up on Google Maps. A campaign gets an overview map plus detail maps. Fewer, clearer maps beat crowded ones.
3. **Build geography:** write `tools/geo/maps/<event-id>.json` and run `node tools/geo/build.mjs tools/geo/maps/<event-id>.json`.
   - `detail`: `local` (< ~60 km wide), `regional` (~60–300 km), `campaign` (larger). The bbox you build should equal the bbox you render.
   - Keep the bbox aspect ratio between about 0.6 and 1.3 (height/width) so maps work on phones.
4. **Check for anachronisms:** `node tools/geo/inspect.mjs <map-id>` lists the big water bodies and stream names. Canals and reservoirs are already removed automatically. Hide dammed lakes, quarry lakes and similar with `water: { hide: [names], hideIn: [[w,s,e,n], ...] }`. Fix historical shorelines with `corrections` (see below). Major known cases:
   - **Boston 1775:** the Shawmut peninsula was almost an island, joined by the narrow Boston Neck. Back Bay, the South End, South Boston flats and much of the waterfront were later landfill. Add water polygons.
   - **Manhattan 1776:** the shoreline lay well inland of today's on both rivers, especially lower Manhattan and the East River side. Battery Park City and the edges of the FDR Drive are landfill.
   - Check other places too (Philadelphia waterfront, Charleston, Yorktown, Newport, etc.).
5. **Write the page and render configs**, then screenshot:
   `node tools/shot.mjs <scratch-dir> events/<event-id>.html` (use your own scratch subdirectory for any helper scripts)
   This prints console/HTTP errors and writes desktop and phone PNGs. **Look at both screenshots** (Read the PNG) and iterate until labels don't collide, nothing important is clipped, and the map reads clearly at phone width.

## Page rules

- **No narrative.** Each map gets a short `<h2>` title, a `<figcaption>` of 1–3 sentences, optionally a short numbered list keyed to callouts on the map, and a `note-approx` line when positions are approximate or schematic.
- The header shows the title, dates and location only. Don't add a lede paragraph.
- Order the maps chronologically.
- Units: miles in text. The scale bar shows miles and km.
- Mark uncertainty honestly: `approx: true` on moves, and say so in the caption note.
- Side colors are fixed by the library. Use the side keys: `continental`, `militia`, `british`, `hessian`, `loyalist`, `french`, `native`, `neutral`.

## Render config reference (`HMap.render(selector, cfg)`)

All coordinates are `[lon, lat]`. Anywhere a coordinate is accepted, you can pass a place id string from `data/places.json` instead.

```js
{
  geo: 'map-id',                   // data/geo/<map-id>.topo.json + .elev.json
  bbox: [w, s, e, n],              // view extent (normally identical to the build spec)
  alt: 'description for screen readers',
  terrain: { contours: 5 | false, hillshade: true, exaggeration: 4, shadeOpacity: 0.55 } | false,
  water: { hide: ['Carnegie Lk'], hideIn: [[w,s,e,n]], hideUnnamed: false, only: ['Hudson Riv', ...] /* named polygons not listed are hidden; unnamed kept */ },
  rivers: { hide: ['Name'], only: ['Name', ...] },
  corrections: { water: [ [[lon,lat], ...] ], land: [ [[lon,lat], ...] ] }, // period shoreline fixes (rings, any winding)
  roads:   [{ coords: [...], name: 'Post Road', kind: 'road'|'track', labelAt: 0.5 }],
  areas:   [{ coords: [...ring], side, label, opacity, legend: 'Legend text', smooth: true }],
  lines:   [{ coords: [...], color, width, dash: '6 4', legend }],
  works:   [{ coords: [...], side, kind: 'line'|'redoubt', closed: false, size }], // fortifications
  towns:   [{ place: 'trenton' } | { name, coords, kind: 'town'|'village'|'building'|'church'|'ferry'|'fort'|'hq', side, label: { dx, dy, anchor } }],
  moves:   [{ side, coords: [...], kind: 'march'|'attack'|'retreat'|'naval', label, labelAt: 0.5, approx, straight, width }],
  units:   [{ side, coords, label, type: 'infantry'|'cavalry'|'artillery', angle, w, h, labelPos: { dx, dy, anchor } }],
  ships:   [{ side, coords, label, angle, labelPos }],
  battles: [{ coords, label, labelPos }],
  labels:  [{ coords, text, kind: 'water'|'region'|'terrain'|'note', angle, size, anchor, dx, dy }],  // '\n' for line breaks
  callouts:[{ coords, n: 1 }],
  legendExtra: [{ svg: '<svg viewBox="0 0 26 12">…</svg>', text: '…' }],
  legend: false,                   // to suppress the auto legend
  textScale: 1,                    // global label size factor
  after: ({ svg, root, defs, proj, P, fs, u, d3 }) => { /* one-off custom drawing */ },
}
```

Notes:
- Label offsets (`dx`/`dy`) are in viewBox units. The map is 1000 units wide.
- Move paths are smoothed through the points; use `straight: true` for straight segments. Labels follow the path and are flipped automatically so they're never upside down.
- Point labels are nudged back inside the frame automatically, but place them well yourself.
- Roads: draw only period roads that matter to the story, from historical maps. Don't trace modern highways.
